title: The lad — voice master (neutral, §24I)
line: You’re alright, you’re alright. I’ve got you. Is your dad alright? He looked like he was going to go over. You alright, sir?
prompt: INGREDIENTS. @image1 is the lad: face, age, hair and build only. These references set what things ARE; the prose below sets what HAPPENS, and nothing in them is a shot to cut to. A plain medium close-up of the lad, a young man of nineteen, standing against a plain light grey-green wall, soft daylight from the left, the camera on a locked tripod, nothing else in frame. The lad looks just off the lens at someone beside the camera and, starting straight away, says these sentences one after another, clearly and completely, with only an ordinary breath between them: "You’re alright, you’re alright. I’ve got you. Is your dad alright? He looked like he was going to go over. You alright, sir?" He keeps speaking from the first second to the last; no long silences. Delivery: A young Londoner of nineteen from south London: a quick, light, friendly voice, London vowels, kind and easy, a little breathless when he has been running. Natural and unforced. Level, even and unhurried; conversational volume; no emotion coloured into the words; a person reading a sentence aloud to themselves. Audio is clean, close production dialogue sound: clear and even, with a little of the room's natural tone behind the voice. Breath and mouth detail are present but never exaggerated. No phone-microphone proximity, no compression pumping, no music and no sound effects anywhere in the clip — dialogue only.
